findings.title: Admin: Mod can approve, overwrite, or clear Admin: Top Style Guide decisions via status normalization bypass
findings.subsystem: S6: Feature controls & Style Guide admin workspace
findings.what_is_wrong: `saveStyleGuideAdminUpdates` (`POST /api/admin/style-guide/save`) enforces `Admin: Top` re-verification using un-trimmed status strings and ignores transitions away from or inheriting an existing `approved` / `not_applicable` status, allowing `Admin: Mod` callers to approve decisions, spoof `approved_by`, overwrite Top-approved values, or wipe Top approvals.
findings.evidence: In `lib/style-guide-admin.js:956-965`, `needsTopForApproval` checks `u && (u.status === 'approved' || u.status === 'not_applicable')` BEFORE `.trim()`. At `line 1004`, `const nextStatus = typeof item.status === 'string' ? item.status.trim() : prevDec.status;` trims trailing whitespace (`"approved "` -> `"approved"`) and defaults omitted `item.status` to `prevDec.status` (`"approved"`). At `lines 1037-1049`, `nextDec.approved_by` accepts caller-supplied `item.approved_by` without restricting to `actorEmail`, and overwriting a previously `approved` decision with `status: "draft"` or `"unanswered"` and `confirm_overwrite: true` never requires `minRole: "top"`.
findings.expected_behavior: Only a re-verified `Admin: Top` (`reverifyPlatformAdminInTx(tx, { ..., minRole: "top" })`) may transition any decision into, within, or out of `approved` / `not_applicable` status, and `approved_by` must be server-derived or constrained to verified governance actors.
findings.actual_condition: An authenticated `Admin: Mod` session can send `POST /api/admin/style-guide/save` with `{"updates":[{"decision_id":"DEC-BRAND-001","status":"approved ","value":"...","approved_by":"any-label"}]}` to mint `approved` decisions without triggering `reverifyPlatformAdminInTx(minRole: "top")`, omit `status` (`confirm_overwrite: true`) to mutate an already-`approved` value while preserving `status: "approved"`, or set `status: "unanswered"` (`confirm_overwrite: true`) to erase Top-approved decisions.
findings.impact: Direct privilege escalation across the documented `Admin: Mod` -> `Admin: Top` RBAC boundary (`docs/engineering/AUTH-AND-PERMISSIONS.md`), integrity compromise of canonical design-system tokens, and spoofed approval attribution.
findings.root_cause: Authorization pre-check (`needsTopForApproval`) operated on raw untrimmed request input prior to per-item normalization and failed to inspect `prevDec.status` inside the locked state snapshot.
findings.recommended_remediation: Normalize `item.status` up front and evaluate `needsTopForApproval` against BOTH normalized `nextStatus` AND `prevDec.status` (`approved` / `not_applicable`), requiring `reverifyPlatformAdminInTx(..., { minRole: "top" })` whenever either is `approved` or `not_applicable`, and bind `approved_by` to the verified Top Admin identity.
implementation_steps: In `lib/style-guide-admin.js:950-1010`, trim and validate every `item.status` against `VALID_STATUSES` before authorization checks.

After loading the locked `prevDecisions` snapshot (`lines 975-995`), check whether any update has `prevDec.status` OR `nextStatus` in `["approved", "not_applicable"]`; if so, require `reverifyPlatformAdminInTx(tx, { userId: actorUserId, sessionId: actorSessionId, minRole: "top" })` (throwing `403 TOP_ADMIN_REQUIRED`).
Set `nextDec.approved_by` from the verified Top Admin actor identity (`actorEmail` or canonical handle) rather than trusting arbitrary `item.approved_by` strings.
findings.regression_risks: `Admin: Mod` users editing `unanswered` or `draft` items into `draft` must continue working without `403`; UI tests in `tests/style-guide-admin.integration.cjs` should verify both allowed Mod drafts and blocked Mod approvals/overwrites.
findings.verification_steps: Add integration cases to `tests/style-guide-admin.integration.cjs` asserting `Admin: Mod` receives `403` on `"status": "approved "`, on omitting `status` against an `approved` item, and on resetting an `approved` item to `draft`, then run `npm run test:style-guide:integration`.

findings.title: Synthetic Test Customer account can be granted Admin: Top, defeating last-human-Top lockout protection and crashing /api/admin/test-customer
findings.subsystem: S1: Auth, sessions, age policy & test-customer sandbox
findings.what_is_wrong: `POST /api/admin/accounts/role` does not block synthetic test account `usr_sa_top_admin_test_customer` (`test-customer@sandbox.biteshark.invalid`) from being granted `top` or `mod` in `platform_roles`, and `GET /api/admin/test-customer` executes mutating SQL (`INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE FROM platform_roles`) on an idempotent `GET` route.
findings.evidence: `server/admin-routes.js:4349-4391` validates `targetUserId` existence in `auth_users` without rejecting `SYNTHETIC_TEST_CUSTOMER_USER_ID`. In `migrations/026_urgent_pilot_security_hardening.sql:37-90`, `protect_last_top_admin()` counts active `platform_roles.role = "top"` rows joined to `auth_users WHERE disabled_at IS NULL`—which `usr_sa_top_admin_test_customer` satisfies! Meanwhile, `lib/admin-test-customer.js:128, 214` runs `DELETE FROM platform_roles WHERE user_id = $1` inside `getAdminTestCustomerStatus` (`GET /api/admin/test-customer`).
findings.expected_behavior: Synthetic sandbox accounts (`usr_sa_top_admin_test_customer` / `*.invalid`) must never be eligible for `platform_roles` or `vendor_memberships` grants, must never count toward `protect_last_top_admin()`, and `GET /api/admin/test-customer` must be strictly read-only.
findings.actual_condition: If `usr_sa_top_admin_test_customer` is granted `Admin: Top`, `protect_last_top_admin()` sees `>= 2` eligible Top Admins, allowing the sole real human `Admin: Top` to be demoted or disabled (`permanent human admin lockout`, as `.invalid` cannot receive OTP emails), after which `GET /api/admin/test-customer` crashes with HTTP `500` (`P0001: LAST_TOP_ADMIN_PROTECTED`).
findings.impact: Potential complete loss of human `Admin: Top` governance access requiring root PostgreSQL emergency intervention, plus HTTP `500` failure of the Admin Portal sandbox status endpoint.
findings.root_cause: Migration `026` predated the synthetic test customer account (`lib/admin-test-customer.js`), and `/api/admin/accounts/role` + `/api/admin/vendors` lacked a guard excluding `SYNTHETIC_TEST_CUSTOMER_USER_ID`.
findings.recommended_remediation: Reject `SYNTHETIC_TEST_CUSTOMER_USER_ID` (and `@sandbox.biteshark.invalid`) in `/api/admin/accounts/role`, `/api/admin/accounts/status`, `/api/admin/invitations`, and vendor ownership assignment; make `getAdminTestCustomerStatus` strictly read-only on `GET`; and add an additive migration updating `count_eligible_active_top_admins()` + a `CHECK (user_id <> 'usr_sa_top_admin_test_customer')` constraint on `platform_roles`.
implementation_steps: In `server/admin-routes.js:4349-4560`, reject `targetUserId === SYNTHETIC_TEST_CUSTOMER_USER_ID` with `400 SYNTHETIC_TEST_ACCOUNT_IMMUTABLE` on role grants and account status mutations.

Refactor `getAdminTestCustomerStatus` (`lib/admin-test-customer.js:185-255`) to perform read-only `SELECT` queries on `GET`, reserving `ensureSyntheticTestCustomerInTx` provisioning writes for `POST` (`enter` / `seed` / `reset`).

Author additive migration `030_harden_synthetic_sandbox_and_rls.sql` adding `CHECK (user_id <> 'usr_sa_top_admin_test_customer')` on `platform_roles` and excluding `usr_sa_top_admin_test_customer` inside `count_eligible_active_top_admins()`.
findings.dependencies: Coordinate migration sequence number `030` across active branches per `docs/engineering/MIGRATIONS.md`.
findings.regression_risks: `GET /api/admin/test-customer` before first `enter` on a brand-new database must cleanly return `counts: { favorites: 0, visits: 0, photos: 0, trails: 0, collections: 0, active_shares: 0 }` when the synthetic user row does not yet exist.
findings.verification_steps: Extend `tests/admin-test-customer.integration.cjs` to assert `POST /api/admin/accounts/role` targeting `usr_sa_top_admin_test_customer` returns `400`, `GET /api/admin/test-customer` executes zero writes on fresh DBs, and the last human Top Admin cannot be demoted.

findings.title: feature_controls untrusted DB state fails OPEN on read_when_not_hidden routes, staff_beta gates, and /s/<token> unlisted shares
findings.subsystem: S6: Feature controls & Style Guide admin workspace
findings.what_is_wrong: When `feature_controls` cannot be read from PostgreSQL OR contains even a single unrecognized `feature_key` row (e.g., after rolling back a newer application release against an additive DB schema), `lib/feature-controls.js` marks `stateUntrusted = true`, discards all persisted `hidden` states and `staff_beta` audience restrictions, substitutes `paused` (or `enabled` for read-only features like `customer_profile`), and allows all `read_when_not_hidden` endpoints and live `/s/<token>` shares to proceed.
findings.evidence: `lib/feature-controls.js:1236` sets `unknownKeys.push(key)` when `!FEATURE_REGISTRY_BY_KEY.has(key)` and `lines 1305-1310` set `stateUntrusted = true` if `unknownKeys.length > 0`. At `lines 1422-1425`, `if (stateUntrusted)` sets `systemEffectiveState = def.allowed_states.includes('paused') ? 'paused' : def.safe_default_state` (`'enabled'` for `customer_profile` and `editorial_stories`!) and skips `configuredAudience === 'staff_beta'` (`line 1428`). Because `enforceRouteFeatureGate` (`lines 1876-1928`) blocks `read_when_not_hidden` ONLY when `state === 'hidden'`, and `lib/customer-profile.js:3014-3019, 4291-4297` blocks `/s/<token>` ONLY when `system_state === 'hidden'`, every hidden read surface fails OPEN.
findings.expected_behavior: Unknown `feature_key` rows from newer additive releases must be ignored (logged as a warning) without invalidating known `feature_controls` rows, and true DB read failures (`stateUntrusted`) must fail CLOSED (`503 FEATURE_STATE_UNAVAILABLE` / neutral `404` on `/s/<token>`) for non-core/beta/sharing surfaces rather than exposing `hidden` or `staff_beta` features.
findings.actual_condition: Rolling back one application release after adding a new `feature_controls` key—or experiencing a transient DB query error—instantly exposes every `hidden` and `staff_beta` feature across `/api/me/profile*`, `/api/me/collections*`, `/api/me/visits`, `/api/me/photos*`, `/api/me/trails`, `/api/stories`, `/api/trails/suggest`, `/s/<token>`, and `/s/<token>/photo/<attachment>`.
findings.impact: Kill-switches (`hidden`) and `staff_beta` access boundaries fail open during rollbacks or transient database errors, exposing emergency-suppressed features and unlisted shared pages/photos.
findings.root_cause: Over-strict `unknownKeys` validation poisoned the entire `feature_controls` snapshot, combined with a fallback state (`paused`/`safe_default_state`) that only blocks mutations while leaving `read_when_not_hidden` and `/s/<token>` open.
findings.recommended_remediation: Ignore unknown `feature_key` rows for known features (recording a diagnostic warning without setting `stateUntrusted = true`), and when `stateUntrusted === true` due to an actual DB read error or invalid known row, fail closed (`503` on API reads for optional/sharing features and neutral `404` on `/s/<token>`).
implementation_steps: In `lib/feature-controls.js:1235-1312`, log/report `unknownKeys` via diagnostics for rollback visibility, but do NOT set `stateUntrusted = true` solely because `unknownKeys.length > 0`; continue honoring validated rows for all known `FEATURE_REGISTRY_BY_KEY` keys.

When `stateUntrusted === true` (actual DB read error or corrupted row on a known key), set effective state for non-essential/sharing features (`unlisted_collection_sharing`, `shared_collection_photos`, `greatest_hits_collections`, `customer_profile`, `admin_style_guide_workspace`) to fail closed (`503` / `hidden`) rather than `enabled`/`paused`.

Check `featureStates.stateUntrusted` in `resolveLiveSharedCollectionByToken` and `readSharedCollectionPhotoByToken` (`lib/customer-profile.js:3014, 4291`) to return the neutral unavailable response on untrusted state.
findings.dependencies: Review `tests/feature-controls.integration.cjs` assertions on `unknownKeys` / `stateUntrusted` behavior before updating.
findings.regression_risks: Core public truck catalog browsing (`public_discovery` / `/api/trucks`) is intentionally resilient during DB degradation; preserve public catalog availability while failing closed on gated account/sharing/beta surfaces.
findings.verification_steps: In `tests/feature-controls.integration.cjs`, insert a `feature_controls` row with `feature_key = "future_release_key"` while `unlisted_collection_sharing = "hidden"`, and assert `/s/<token>` and `/api/me/shares/create` remain blocked (`404`/`403`). Also simulate a DB query failure on `feature_controls` and verify `/s/<token>` fails closed.

findings.title: Invalid write-pause scope "favorites" in api/favorites/toggle.js triggers fail-closed global write outage when configured
findings.subsystem: S2: HTTP server core, routing, api/* handlers & DB adapter
findings.what_is_wrong: `api/favorites/toggle.js` calls `enforceWritePause(req, "favorites")`, but `"favorites"` is not in `VALID_PAUSE_SCOPES` in `lib/authz.js`. Setting `BITESHARK_PAUSE_WRITES=favorites` causes `parsePauseWritesEnv()` to flag an invalid token and set `failClosedAll = true`, halting ALL writes across the entire application (`503`).
findings.evidence: `api/favorites/toggle.js:10`: `const paused = enforceWritePause(req, 'favorites');`. `lib/authz.js:120-127`: `const VALID_PAUSE_SCOPES = new Set(['all', 'bookings', 'owner', 'pager', 'community', 'notifications']);` (`'favorites'` is missing!). `lib/authz.js:169-174`: `if (!VALID_PAUSE_SCOPES.has(part)) { invalidTokens.push(part); } ... failClosedAll: invalidTokens.length > 0` -> every `enforceWritePause` call returns `503 WRITE_PAUSED`.
findings.expected_behavior: `VALID_PAUSE_SCOPES` must include `"favorites"` (and any other domain scope passed to `enforceWritePause`) so operators can granularly pause favorites writes without triggering an accidental sitewide write outage, while `BITESHARK_PAUSE_WRITES=all` continues pausing `favorites`.
findings.actual_condition: Granularly pausing favorites via `BITESHARK_PAUSE_WRITES=favorites` immediately takes down bookings, owner updates, pickup pagers, community posts, notifications, and admin/customer writes that check `enforceWritePause`.
findings.impact: Severe operational self-DoS trap during incident response when an operator attempts to pause only favorites writes.
findings.root_cause: `api/favorites/toggle.js` was wired with scope `"favorites"` without registering `"favorites"` in `VALID_PAUSE_SCOPES` in `lib/authz.js`.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add `"favorites"` (plus `"exploration"`, `"profile"`, `"governance"`, `"issues"` when expanding `PAUSE_WRITES` in `AUD-0014`) to `VALID_PAUSE_SCOPES` in `lib/authz.js` and document all supported scopes in `docs/VPS_OPERATIONS.md` and `configuration-keys.json`.
implementation_steps: Add `"favorites"` to `VALID_PAUSE_SCOPES` in `lib/authz.js:120-127`.
Add a runtime assertion or unit check inside `enforceWritePause(req, scope)` warning in tests if a caller passes a `scope` absent from `VALID_PAUSE_SCOPES`.
Update `docs/VPS_OPERATIONS.md` with the exact list of valid `BITESHARK_PAUSE_WRITES` scopes.
findings.dependencies: Coordinate with `REP-009` (`AUD-0014`) so all write-pause scopes are registered in one place.
findings.regression_risks: None; preserves fail-closed behavior for genuinely misspelled operator env tokens while making `"favorites"` work as intended.
findings.verification_steps: Add a test in `tests/backend-hardening.integration.cjs` setting `BITESHARK_PAUSE_WRITES=favorites` and asserting `POST /api/favorites/toggle` returns `503` while `POST /api/bookings/create` and `POST /api/pager/create` remain `200`/`201`.

findings.title: Shared-collection moderation suppression can be bypassed via photo re-attachment, collection updates, and multi-share disclosure masking
findings.subsystem: S4: Customer profile, Greatest Hits sharing, exploration & photos
findings.what_is_wrong: Three moderation enforcement bypasses exist in `lib/customer-profile.js`: (1) after `suppress_attachment`, the owner can call `POST /api/me/collections/attach-photo` with the exact same `source_photo_id` to mint a fresh `moderation_status = "active"` `sha_*` derivative (while revoking/deleting the suppressed attachment needed by moderators); (2) `computeCollectionContentDigest` ignores `photo_attachment_id` and `SUPPRESSED_CONTENT_BYPASS_BLOCKED` is never checked in `updateOwnerCollection`; and (3) `listAdminSharedModerationQueue` reads disclosure flags solely from `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1` (`latestShare`), hiding curator `display_name`/`bio` still live on an older reported link.
findings.evidence: `lib/customer-profile.js:4013-4062, 4121-4150` checks `colRes.rows[0].moderation_status === "suppressed"` but never checks if `previousAttachmentId` or `(user_id, recorded_source_photo_id)` / `sha256_hex` was suppressed, setting `revoked_at` on the prior attachment (which causes `readAdminReportedSharedPhoto` at `line 4461` to reject moderator inspection!). `lines 1478-1488` hash only `{ title, intro, entries: [{ v, r }] }`, and `updateOwnerCollection` (`lines 1866-2034`) performs zero `suppressed_content_sha256` checks. `lines 3567-3621` query `LIMIT 1` for `latestShare` despite `MAX_ACTIVE_SHARES_PER_COLLECTION = 3`.
findings.expected_behavior: Suppressed photos (`recorded_source_photo_id` or `sha256_hex`) must remain blocked from re-attachment until `Admin: Top` executes `reinstate_attachment`; suppressed collection content must not be editable onto an already-shared collection; and moderator previews must union disclosures across all active/reported shares.
findings.actual_condition: Collection owners can immediately republish Moderator- or Top-Admin-suppressed photos and text onto live `/s/<token>` URLs and obscure abusive profile disclosures from moderators.
findings.impact: Defeats content moderation and `Admin: Top` reinstatement controls on public-reachable unlisted `/s/<token>` pages and destroys moderator evidence files.
findings.root_cause: Suppression checks were added to `createCollectionShareLink` and `reinstate_attachment` without guarding `attachPhotoToCollectionEntry`, `updateOwnerCollection`, or multi-link disclosure aggregation.
findings.recommended_remediation: Block re-attaching suppressed `recorded_source_photo_id` / `sha256_hex` in `attachPhotoToCollectionEntry` (and retain suppressed `sha_*` files while referenced by moderation actions), enforce `suppressed_content_sha256` (including attachment digests) inside `updateOwnerCollection` when shares exist, and union disclosure booleans across all active/reported shares in `listAdminSharedModerationQueue`.
implementation_steps: In `attachPhotoToCollectionEntry` (`lib/customer-profile.js:4013-4150`), query `customer_collection_photo_attachments` for `user_id = $1 AND moderation_status = 'suppressed' AND (recorded_source_photo_id = $2 OR sha256_hex = $3)` and throw `403 PHOTO_SUPPRESSED_BY_MODERATION`; do not unlink a prior `sha_*` file when `moderation_status = 'suppressed'`.

Include `photo_attachment_id` / `sha256_hex` in `computeCollectionContentDigest` (`line 1478`) and check `suppressed_content_sha256` inside `updateOwnerCollection` (`lines 1950-2020`) whenever the collection has active shares.

In `listAdminSharedModerationQueue` (`lines 3567-3621`), compute `include_display_name`, `include_bio`, `include_preferred_area`, and `include_shared_photos` using `BOOL_OR(...)` across all active or reported shares on the collection.
findings.regression_risks: Owners should still be permitted to remove a suppressed entry or attach a *different* non-suppressed photo if only the single photo (not the whole collection) was suppressed.
findings.verification_steps: Add integration tests in `tests/customer-profile-sharing.integration.cjs` covering all three bypass vectors and run `npm run test:profile`.

findings.title: Under-14 birth date submission on POST /api/me/sharing-eligibility rolls back without locking eligibility or revoking session
findings.subsystem: S4: Customer profile, Greatest Hits sharing, exploration & photos
findings.what_is_wrong: In `submitAdultSharingEligibility`, ages 14–17 commit `eligibility_status = "ineligible_under_18"` inside `withTransaction` before throwing `403` outside the transaction so the user cannot retry with a fake adult DOB. When `evalRes.under_14` is true (`< 14`), however, `CustomerProfileDomainError` is thrown *inside* `withTransaction`, rolling back the transaction and leaving `customer_sharing_eligibility` at `"unknown"` and the session active.
findings.evidence: `lib/customer-profile.js:2263-2268`: `if (evalRes.under_14) { throw new CustomerProfileDomainError(evalRes.error, { status: 403, code: 'AGE_INELIGIBLE' }); }` inside `withTransaction` (triggers `ROLLBACK`), whereas `lines 2271-2292` (`!evalRes.eligible_18_plus` for 14–17) `INSERT INTO customer_sharing_eligibility ... VALUES ($1, 'ineligible_under_18', ...)` and return `{ deniedError }` so `withTransaction` commits before throwing at `line 2305`.
findings.expected_behavior: Submitting an under-14 birth date must commit a durable ineligible state (never leaving `customer_sharing_eligibility` retryable as `"unknown"`) and align with BiteShark's 14+ account age policy (`docs/engineering/AUTH-AND-PERMISSIONS.md`) regarding session revocation / account suspension without storing raw DOB.
findings.actual_condition: A user submitting a 12-year-old birth date receives `403 AGE_INELIGIBLE`, retains an active session and `"unknown"` sharing eligibility, and can immediately submit `1995-01-01` on the very next request to unlock 18+ external link sharing.
findings.impact: Under-14 age-policy compliance gap on external sharing eligibility.
findings.root_cause: Throwing `CustomerProfileDomainError` inside `withTransaction` aborted the transaction instead of using the commit-then-throw `{ deniedError }` pattern used immediately below for ages 14–17.
findings.recommended_remediation: Use the commit-then-throw `{ deniedError }` pattern for `evalRes.under_14` so `ineligible_under_18` is always committed in `customer_sharing_eligibility`, and confirm with product/legal whether under-14 self-attestation on `/api/me/sharing-eligibility` should also mark `auth_users.age_eligibility_status = "ineligible"` + disable/revoke active sessions like `/api/auth/age-assessment`.
implementation_steps: In `lib/customer-profile.js:2263-2295`, persist `ineligible_under_18` in `customer_sharing_eligibility` inside `withTransaction` and return `{ deniedError: new CustomerProfileDomainError(evalRes.error, { status: 403, code: "AGE_INELIGIBLE" }) }` so the lock commits before throwing `403`.

Once product/legal confirms account-wide handling (`Decisions Required`), optionally revoke `auth_sessions` and update `auth_users.age_eligibility_status` in the same committed transaction (storing zero raw DOB fields).
findings.dependencies: Product/legal confirmation on whether under-14 sharing-gate input should also suspend the 14+ account or lock sharing eligibility only.
findings.regression_risks: If account-wide session revocation is enabled, ensure `public/greatest-hits-sharing.js` handles `401`/`403 AGE_INELIGIBLE` by clearing client caches and redirecting cleanly.
findings.verification_steps: Add a test in `tests/customer-profile-sharing.integration.cjs` posting a 12-year-old DOB (`403`) followed by a 25-year-old DOB and asserting the second request is rejected (`403`) with `eligibility_status = "ineligible_under_18"`.

findings.title: Unlisted /s/<token> routes ignore staff_beta audience restrictions and two customer/shared endpoints omit central route feature rules
findings.subsystem: S4: Customer profile, Greatest Hits sharing, exploration & photos
findings.what_is_wrong: `greatest_hits_collections`, `unlisted_collection_sharing`, and `shared_collection_photos` all advertise `allowed_audiences: ["all", "staff_beta"]`, where `system_effective_state` remains `"enabled"` and only `caller_effective_state` becomes `"hidden"` for non-staff callers. However, `/s/<token>` and `/s/<token>/photo/<attachment>` pass `verifiedUser = null` and inspect `.system_state === "hidden"`, leaving all shared links publicly viewable during `staff_beta`. Additionally, `GET /api/me/exploration` and `POST /api/shared/report` are absent from `ROUTE_FEATURE_ENFORCEMENT_RULES` in `lib/feature-controls.js`.
findings.evidence: `server/customer-profile-routes.js:727-731, 804-810` call `resolveCallerProfileFeatureFlags(dbAdapter, req, null)` and pass `systemFeatureStates`. `lib/customer-profile.js:3014-3019, 4291-4297` check `systemFeatureStates?.unlisted_collection_sharing?.system_state === 'hidden'`. Meanwhile, `lib/feature-controls.js:1876-1928` (`ROUTE_FEATURE_ENFORCEMENT_RULES`) has no rule for `/api/me/exploration` or `/api/shared/report`.
findings.expected_behavior: Setting `audience: "staff_beta"` must either restrict `/s/<token>` and `/s/<token>/photo/<attachment>` to authenticated `staff_beta` viewers (resolving the viewer session cookie) OR explicitly state in the Admin Feature Controls UI that `staff_beta` restricts link creation only; and `ROUTE_FEATURE_ENFORCEMENT_RULES` should explicitly declare the policy for every exploration/sharing endpoint.
findings.actual_condition: Operators placing sharing features into `staff_beta` leave existing and staff-created `/s/<token>` pages and photos publicly accessible to unauthenticated internet visitors.
findings.impact: Unexpected public exposure of beta features and unlisted shared content when operators configure `audience = "staff_beta"`.
findings.root_cause: Recipient routes passed `null` user context to `resolveCallerProfileFeatureFlags` and checked `system_state` instead of caller `state`.
findings.recommended_remediation: Confirm product intent for `staff_beta` recipient viewing; pass resolved read-only viewer session (`sess?.user || null`) into `resolveCallerProfileFeatureFlags` on both `/s/<token>` and `/s/<token>/photo/<attachment>` to enforce `.state === "hidden"` when `staff_beta` is active, and register explicit entries (or documented exemptions) for `GET /api/me/exploration` and `POST /api/shared/report` in `lib/feature-controls.js`.
implementation_steps: In `server/app.js:1330-1360`, resolve read-only viewer session on `/s/<token>/photo/<attachment>` (without sliding-window cookie mutation) just as `/s/<token>` already does at `line 1345`, and forward `viewerUser: sess?.user || null` to both handlers.

In `server/customer-profile-routes.js:727, 804` and `lib/customer-profile.js:3014, 4291`, pass `viewerUser` to `resolveCallerProfileFeatureFlags` and gate on `.state === "hidden"` (or document explicit `staff_beta` semantics in `lib/feature-controls.js:419-455` per product decision).
Add explicit route metadata in `lib/feature-controls.js:1876-1928` for `/api/me/exploration` and `/api/shared/report`.
findings.dependencies: Product decision on whether `staff_beta` on `unlisted_collection_sharing` should require recipients of `/s/<token>` to be signed-in staff.
findings.regression_risks: If `/s/<token>` requires staff sign-in during `staff_beta`, incognito recipient tests under `staff_beta` will receive the neutral `404` page by design.
findings.verification_steps: Add a `staff_beta` recipient test in `tests/customer-profile-sharing.integration.cjs` verifying anonymous vs staff `GET /s/<token>` and `GET /s/<token>/photo/<att>`.

findings.title: Admin: Mod can enumerate masked customer emails via /api/admin/accounts ILIKE oracle and read unmasked emails and Top-only telemetry on /api/admin/invitations & /api/admin/audit
findings.subsystem: S3: Admin governance backend
findings.what_is_wrong: Per `docs/engineering/AUTH-AND-PERMISSIONS.md`, `Admin: Mod` is restricted from viewing raw customer PII (`maskEmail` on `/api/admin/accounts`) and Top-only diagnostic/provider telemetry. However: (1) `GET /api/admin/accounts?q=...` runs unescaped SQL `u.email_normalized ILIKE $N` *before* applying `maskEmail`, allowing `Admin: Mod` to reconstruct any customer email character-by-character; (2) `GET /api/admin/invitations` returns unmasked `recipient_email` for `customer_access` invites plus Top-only provider error codes/IDs to `Admin: Mod`; and (3) `GET /api/admin/audit` leaks Top-restricted `diagnostic_group_id` and `fixing_release_sha` inside `issue.diagnostic_*` metadata.
findings.evidence: `server/admin-routes.js:4222, 4247-4250, 4309`: filters `u.email_normalized ILIKE '%' || q || '%'` (with unescaped `_` and `%` wildcards) and only masks `email: ctx.isTopAdmin ? r.email : maskEmail(r.email)` during serialization. `server/admin-routes.js:4660` & `lib/admin-governance.js:301-326`: `GET /api/admin/invitations` allows `Mod` and returns raw `recipient_email`, `last_provider_message_id`, and `last_delivery_error_code`. `server/admin-routes.js:7240-7244` returns raw `audit_logs.metadata` on `issue.diagnostic_linked` without redacting `diagnostic_group_id` / `fixing_release_sha` (which `/api/admin/issues` explicitly strips for `Mod` at `lines 6595-6601`).
findings.expected_behavior: `Admin: Mod` searches on `/api/admin/accounts` must not match hidden characters of customer emails (search by `user_id`, exact email hash/domain, or staff/vendor emails only, with escaped `ILIKE`), customer emails and provider telemetry on `/api/admin/invitations` must be masked/redacted for `Mod`, and `/api/admin/audit` must strip Top-only diagnostic metadata for `Mod`.
findings.actual_condition: An `Admin: Mod` account can de-anonymize any customer email via prefix/wildcard queries on `/api/admin/accounts?q=` and read raw customer emails and Top-only diagnostic/provider identifiers via `/api/admin/invitations` and `/api/admin/audit`.
findings.impact: Violates `Admin: Mod` least-privilege PII and diagnostic isolation contracts.
findings.root_cause: Masking/redaction was applied inconsistently at individual endpoint serializers without auditing SQL filter side-channels or cross-endpoint projections (`/api/admin/invitations`, `/api/admin/audit`).
findings.recommended_remediation: Restrict `Admin: Mod` `q` matching on `/api/admin/accounts` so non-staff customer emails are only matched on `u.id` or masked-safe domain/exact match (and escape `ILIKE` wildcards across all admin search routes), mask `customer_access` `recipient_email` + redact provider telemetry for `Mod` in `/api/admin/invitations`, and scrub Top-only diagnostic keys from `/api/admin/audit` for `Mod`.
implementation_steps: Centralize `escapeSqlLike(q)` in `lib/admin-governance.js` and apply `ESCAPE '\\'` across all admin `ILIKE` filters (`server/admin-routes.js:3286, 3799, 4222, 5303, 6619, 7229`).

In `server/admin-routes.js:4247-4252`, when `!ctx.isTopAdmin`, restrict email `ILIKE` matching to accounts holding `platform_roles` or `vendor_memberships` (allowing `u.id` lookup or exact-email match for customer accounts).

In `lib/admin-governance.js:301-326` / `server/admin-routes.js:4660`, mask `recipient_email` on `customer_access` invitations and omit `last_provider_message_id` / raw provider error details when `!ctx.isTopAdmin`; in `server/admin-routes.js:7240-7244`, strip `diagnostic_group_id` and `fixing_release_sha` from `audit_logs.metadata` when `!ctx.isTopAdmin`.
findings.regression_risks: Ensure `Admin: Mod` can still look up a customer account by `user_id` (`usr_...`) when triaging a support issue.
findings.verification_steps: Add assertions in `tests/admin-governance.integration.cjs` confirming `Admin: Mod` cannot probe substring matches on a customer email via `/api/admin/accounts?q=`, receives masked `customer_access` emails on `/api/admin/invitations`, and sees redacted diagnostic metadata on `/api/admin/audit`.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/diagnostics/report can evict server_verified incidents (cascading issue links), spoof actor_id, and bypass secret/cookie regex scrubbers
findings.subsystem: S5: Pager notifications, Web Push worker & diagnostics
findings.what_is_wrong: Multiple security/forensic weaknesses exist in diagnostics & log redaction: (1) `POST /api/diagnostics/report` accepts unauthenticated `browser_untrusted` telemetry into the same `500`-row `diagnostic_incident_groups` eviction pool as `server_verified` incidents (`ON DELETE CASCADE` deleting `support_issue_diagnostic_links`); (2) `POST /api/diagnostics/report` preserves caller-supplied `safe_context.actor_id` on unauthenticated reports; (3) `lib/diagnostics.js` uses `\b` before `secret|token|password` (which fails to match underscore-prefixed keys like `auth_secret=`, `unsubscribe_token=`, `session_token=`, `db_password=` because `_` is a word character!) and `{34,}` misses 22-char `auth_secret` and 32-char `unsubscribe_token`; (4) `public/diagnostics-client.js` omits JWT, UUID, and session-cookie scrubbers; and (5) `deploy/bin/biteshark-staging2-ctl` redacts `__Host-truckly_session=` but omits `__Host-bs_admin_test_session=`.
findings.evidence: `lib/diagnostics.js:1010-1021` evicts `WHERE status IN ('resolved', 'ignored')` then falls back to evicting ANY oldest group across the shared 500-group cap, triggering `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `support_issue_diagnostic_links` (`migrations/025:429`). `lib/diagnostics.js:87, 169, 182` uses `\b(?:password|secret|token)` (fails after `_`) and `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{34,}` (misses 22–32 char secrets). `server/admin-routes.js:709` spreads `body.safe_context` before setting `actor_id` only if authenticated. `deploy/bin/biteshark-staging2-ctl:144` matches only `__Host-truckly_session=`.
findings.expected_behavior: Untrusted browser telemetry must be capped in a separate quota that can NEVER evict `server_verified` groups or issue-linked groups; `browser_untrusted` reports must overwrite `actor_id` strictly from verified session state; and all server/client/CLI redactors must scrub underscore-prefixed `*_secret`/`*_token`/`*_password` keys, 22+ char secrets, and `__Host-bs_admin_test_session` cookies.
findings.actual_condition: External scripts rotating `error_code` across IP windows can evict `server_verified` auth/security incidents and unlink open support tickets, forge `actor_id` in untrusted payloads, and leak `auth_secret=`/`unsubscribe_token=` or `__Host-bs_admin_test_session=` in diagnostic/operator logs.
findings.impact: Loss of server security/incident forensics, broken support-issue diagnostic links, log spoofing, and incomplete secret/session redaction.
findings.root_cause: Shared eviction SQL did not partition `trust_source = "browser_untrusted"` from `server_verified` or `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM support_issue_diagnostic_links ...)`, and regex ` ` semantics with `_` (`w`) were overlooked.
findings.recommended_remediation: Partition `browser_untrusted` group eviction (e.g., max 150 untrusted groups, never evicting `server_verified` or linked groups), strip caller `actor_id` on `POST /api/diagnostics/report`, replace `\b` with `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9])` and lower token-entropy length bounds in `lib/diagnostics.js` + `public/diagnostics-client.js`, and add `__Host-bs_admin_test_session` redaction to `deploy/bin/biteshark-staging2-ctl` and `deploy/install-staging-release.sh`.
implementation_steps: In `lib/diagnostics.js:1008-1025`, enforce a dedicated cap (e.g., `150`) for `trust_source = 'browser_untrusted'` and add `AND trust_source = 'browser_untrusted' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM support_issue_diagnostic_links l WHERE l.diagnostic_group_id = diagnostic_incident_groups.id)` when evicting for untrusted inserts; protect issue-linked `server_verified` groups from eviction as well.
In `server/admin-routes.js:695-712`, strip `actor_id`, `actor_role`, and `session_id` from incoming `body.safe_context` and populate `actor_id` exclusively from verified `req.user?.id || null`.

In `lib/diagnostics.js:85-190`, replace `\b` before sensitive key names with `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9]|_)` and scrub `__Host-bs_admin_test_session` + 22+ char base64url tokens; mirror cookie/JWT/UUID scrubbers in `public/diagnostics-client.js:69-82` and `__Host-bs_admin_test_session=` in `deploy/bin/biteshark-staging2-ctl:144` & `deploy/install-staging-release.sh:737`.
findings.regression_risks: Ensure lowering high-entropy token redaction thresholds does not redact short normal slugs (`mitote`, `DEC-BRAND-001`) or `corr_*` correlation IDs.
findings.verification_steps: Add unit/integration assertions in `tests/diagnostics-and-reliability.integration.cjs` and `tests/staging2-ctl-security.test.cjs` testing `auth_secret=`, `unsubscribe_token=`, `__Host-bs_admin_test_session=`, `actor_id` spoofing, and `browser_untrusted` flood isolation.

findings.title: Third-party CDN Leaflet script & stylesheet load without Subresource Integrity (SRI) and block all first-party scripts, while HTML pages lack baseline CSP
findings.subsystem: S7: Customer-facing SPA frontend
findings.what_is_wrong: `public/index.html` loads `https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.css` (`line 7`) and synchronous `<script src="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js"></script>` (`line 459`) without `integrity="sha384-..."` or `crossorigin=""` attributes, directly on the same origin that hosts authenticated customer, vendor, and `/admin` sessions (`__Host-truckly_session`), and ahead of all 18 first-party scripts. Furthermore, `applyBaselineSecurityHeaders` (`server/app.js:248-252`) sets no `Content-Security-Policy` on `/`, `/admin`, `/login.html`, or `/policies/*` (unlike `/s/<token>`, which enforces strict CSP).
findings.evidence: `public/index.html:7`: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.css">`. `public/index.html:459`: `<script src="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js"></script>` (no `integrity`, no `crossorigin`, no `defer`, even when `interactive_map` is `hidden`!). `server/app.js:248-252` sets only `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, and `Permissions-Policy`.
findings.expected_behavior: Third-party CDN scripts/stylesheets must either be vendored locally under `public/vendor/leaflet/` (eliminating external runtime dependency and render-blocking stalls) or pinned with SHA-384 Subresource Integrity (`integrity` + `crossorigin="anonymous"`), and `/admin` + `/login.html` + `/` should carry an explicit `Content-Security-Policy` (`object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'self'`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`).
findings.actual_condition: Compromise of `unpkg.com` grants full JavaScript execution across BiteShark's origin without SRI verification; slow/blackholed TCP connections to `unpkg.com` block execution of all 18 local scripts until browser script timeout; and `/admin` lacks `Content-Security-Policy`.
findings.impact: Third-party CDN supply-chain XSS exposure across authenticated customer/vendor sessions and single-point-of-failure render blocking when `unpkg.com` hangs.
findings.root_cause: Early prototype CDN `<link>`/`<script>` tags in `public/index.html` were retained while map-tile resilience was added inside `public/app.js`.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add cryptographic `integrity` + `crossorigin="anonymous"` attributes to Leaflet CSS/JS immediately (or vendor Leaflet 1.9.4 locally in `public/vendor/leaflet/` and lazy-load only when `interactive_map` is not hidden), and add a strict `Content-Security-Policy` header to `/admin` and `/login.html` (where zero inline event handlers exist) plus a compatible `object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'` baseline CSP on `/`.
implementation_steps: Add exact SHA-384 `integrity` and `crossorigin="anonymous"` attributes to `public/index.html:7` and `public/index.html:459` (or vendor `leaflet.js`, `leaflet.css`, and marker PNGs locally under `public/vendor/leaflet/`).
Load Leaflet non-blockingly (`defer` or dynamic loader in `public/app.js` gated on `!isFeatureHidden("interactive_map")`) so an unreachable CDN never stalls first-party script execution.

In `server/app.js`, attach a strict `Content-Security-Policy` (`default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; connect-src 'self' https://api.github.com; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`) on `/admin` and `/login.html`, and baseline `object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'` across all HTML responses.
findings.dependencies: Verify `tests/map-resilience.test.cjs` and `tests/map-resilience-browser.e2e.cjs` expectations on Leaflet `<script>` tags before changing URL vs adding SRI.
findings.regression_risks: `public/index.html` and `public/app.js` currently use inline `onclick="..."` attributes (`openDetail`, `closeModal`), so `/` cannot set `script-src 'self'` without `'unsafe-inline'` until inline handlers are migrated; `/admin` and `/login.html` use zero inline `on*` handlers (verify before deploying `script-src 'self'`).
findings.verification_steps: Run `node tests/map-resilience.test.cjs`, `tests/map-resilience-browser.e2e.cjs`, and `tests/admin-portal-browser.e2e.cjs`, confirming zero CSP console violations on `/`, `/login.html`, and `/admin`.

findings.title: Community feed (/api/community/list) and post creation (/api/community/post) bypass vendor hidden_from_discovery and deactivation governance
findings.subsystem: S2: HTTP server core, routing, api/* handlers & DB adapter
findings.what_is_wrong: Admin vendor governance (`POST /api/admin/vendors/status`) allows `Admin: Mod` / `Admin: Top` to hide (`hidden_from_discovery = true`) or deactivate (`is_active = false`, `ownership_status = "suspended"`) a vendor. However, `GET /api/community/list` returns all `approved` posts without joining `vendors`, and `POST /api/community/post` checks only `vendors.is_active`, ignoring `hidden_from_discovery` and `ownership_status`.
findings.evidence: `api/community/list.js:8-13`: `SELECT id, place_id, place_name, town, kind, rating, title, body, author_label, created_at FROM community_reviews WHERE status = 'approved' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 80` (no `JOIN vendors` filter). `api/community/post.js:95-103`: queries `SELECT is_active, canonical_name, city FROM vendors WHERE id = $1` and checks only `vRow.is_active === false`, omitting `hidden_from_discovery === true`.
findings.expected_behavior: Vendors suppressed via `hidden_from_discovery = true` or `is_active = false` must be excluded from public `/api/community/list` feeds and rejected (`404`/`403`) for new community submissions in `/api/community/post`, matching `loadDiscoveryCatalog` (`lib/discovery.js`).
findings.actual_condition: Deactivated or hidden businesses remain publicly visible in the Community tab feed, and hidden businesses continue accepting new customer reviews/tips.
findings.impact: Bypasses administrative vendor takedown/suppression controls on the public site.
findings.root_cause: `api/community/list.js` and `api/community/post.js` predated the `hidden_from_discovery` governance flags introduced in Migration `018` and `lib/discovery.js`.
findings.recommended_remediation: Filter `api/community/list.js` against `loadDiscoveryCatalog` (or `LEFT JOIN vendors v ON v.id = community_reviews.place_id WHERE COALESCE(v.is_active, true) = true AND COALESCE(v.hidden_from_discovery, false) = false`) and enforce `!vRow.hidden_from_discovery` (plus catalog existence for unseeded static vendors) in `api/community/post.js`.
implementation_steps: In `api/community/list.js:8-15`, add `LEFT JOIN vendors v ON v.id = community_reviews.place_id` with `AND COALESCE(v.is_active, true) = true AND COALESCE(v.hidden_from_discovery, false) = false` (and verify static-only `place_id`s exist in `TRUCKS`).
In `api/community/post.js:95-105`, select `hidden_from_discovery` alongside `is_active` and reject with `403`/`404` when `vRow.hidden_from_discovery === true`.
findings.regression_risks: Static catalog entries that do not yet have a `vendors` DB row rely on `LEFT JOIN` (`COALESCE(..., true/false)`); test both DB-backed and static-only vendor IDs.
findings.verification_steps: Extend `tests/p1-unified-discovery.integration.cjs` to hide a vendor with an approved community post via `/api/admin/vendors/status` and assert it disappears from `GET /api/community/list` and rejects `POST /api/community/post`.

findings.title: 14 database tables lack FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, api/favorites & notifications execute no-op GUC calls, and favorites/toggle accepts unbounded arbitrary truck_ids
findings.subsystem: S9: Database migrations, RLS policies, schema & indexes
findings.what_is_wrong: Although newer BiteShark tables (`migrations/012`–`029`) enforce `ENABLE` + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, 14 SQL tables (`bookings`, `truck_settings`, `favorites`, `notification_settings`, `owner_profiles`, `owner_schedule`, `pickup_pagers`, `vendors`, `platform_roles`, `vendor_memberships`, `audit_logs`, `platform_role_revocations`, `admin_bootstrap_grants`, `vendor_status_history`, plus `schema_migrations`) have **no RLS enabled or forced**. Worse, `api/favorites/toggle.js:23` and `api/notifications/settings.js:21` execute `SELECT set_config('app.user_id', ...)` against tables that have zero RLS policies (giving a false appearance of DB-enforced tenant isolation), and `api/favorites/toggle.js` accepts any arbitrary string `<= 80` chars as `truck_id` with no catalog/vendor validation, no per-user cap, and no dedicated rate limit.
findings.evidence: `wave2_verified.json` (`sqlSummary.tablesWithoutForceRls`): `0` `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE/FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` statements exist for `bookings`, `favorites`, `notification_settings`, `pickup_pagers`, `owner_profiles`, `owner_schedule`, `truck_settings`, `vendors`, `platform_roles`, `vendor_memberships`, `audit_logs`, `platform_role_revocations`, `admin_bootstrap_grants`, or `vendor_status_history`. In `api/favorites/toggle.js:18-44`, `truckId` checks only `truckId.length > 80` and inserts directly into `favorites (user_id, truck_id)` with no catalog check or row cap.
findings.expected_behavior: User-scoped tables (`favorites`, `notification_settings`, `bookings`) must enforce `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` keyed on `app.user_id` (or documented vendor/admin GUC scopes), `api/favorites/toggle.js` must validate `truck_id` against known discovery/DB vendors with a bounded per-user cap (e.g. `200`) and rate limit, and `DATA-MODEL.md` must accurately distinguish RLS-enforced vs app-mediated governance tables.
findings.actual_condition: Any query bug omitting `WHERE user_id = $1` on `favorites`, `notification_settings`, or `bookings` exposes cross-tenant data, and an authenticated user can stuff unlimited bogus `truck_id` rows into `favorites`.
findings.impact: Missing database-layer tenant isolation on legacy customer/vendor tables and unbounded table-bloat vector on `favorites`.
findings.root_cause: Migrations `001`–`011` and `018` were authored before `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` became the repository standard in Migrations `019`–`029`.
findings.recommended_remediation: Validate `truck_id` against `loadDiscoveryCatalog` / `vendors`, enforce a per-user `favorites` cap (`200`) + rate limit in `api/favorites/toggle.js`, and add an additive migration enabling `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` on `favorites` and `notification_settings` first (where `app.user_id` GUC is already set in `withTransaction` / `packages/runtime-adapter`), followed by scoped policies for `bookings` and `pickup_pagers` after auditing all query paths.
implementation_steps: In `api/favorites/toggle.js`, wrap writes in `withTransaction`, verify `truckId` exists in `TRUCKS` or active `vendors`, enforce `COUNT(*) < 200` on new inserts, and apply a per-user write rate limit.

Audit all callers of `favorites` (`api/favorites/list.js`, `api/favorites/toggle.js`, `lib/customer-profile.js`, `lib/admin-test-customer.js`) to confirm `app.user_id` (or explicit sandbox reset GUC) is set in every transaction, then enable + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` on `favorites` and `notification_settings` in an additive migration.
Document the exact non-RLS governance tables (`platform_roles`, `vendor_memberships`, `audit_logs`) and rationale in `docs/engineering/DATA-MODEL.md`.
findings.dependencies: Run full PostgreSQL integration suite (`backend-hardening`, `p1-unified-discovery`, `customer-profile-sharing`, `admin-test-customer`) before landing RLS on legacy tables—remember `lib/admin-test-customer.js` deletes sandbox `favorites` while `app.user_id` may be the admin unless `app.user_id` is switched or a policy permits sandbox reset!
findings.regression_risks: High if RLS is added to `favorites` without updating `lib/admin-test-customer.js` (`seed`/`reset` queries `favorites` for `usr_sa_top_admin_test_customer`)—verify every SQL caller via `npm run registry:locate -- favorites` first!
findings.verification_steps: Run `node tools/code-registry/cli.mjs validate --verify-db`, `tests/backend-hardening.integration.cjs`, `tests/customer-profile-sharing.integration.cjs`, and `tests/admin-test-customer.integration.cjs`.

findings.title: Concurrent lost-update race in Style Guide push/save overwrites workspace-state.json, and corrupt state JSON silently resets to empty
findings.subsystem: S6: Feature controls & Style Guide admin workspace
findings.what_is_wrong: `pushStyleGuideWorkspaceToGithub` (`POST /api/admin/style-guide/push`) reads `snap = buildEffectiveDecisionsSnapshot()` (`line 1363`) *before* performing 7–10 sequential outbound HTTPS requests to GitHub (`git/ref`, `commits`, `blobs`, `trees`, `commits`, `PATCH ref`), and afterward writes `{ ...snap.wsState, revision: Number(snap.wsState.revision || 0) + 1, last_github_push: pushRecord }` directly over `workspace-state.json` (`lines 1654-1666`) with no process mutex or PostgreSQL advisory lock. Any `POST /api/admin/style-guide/save` completed during that multi-second GitHub push is silently wiped from disk. Additionally, `readWorkspaceState` (`lines 329-349`) catches JSON parse errors and silently returns `emptyState`, causing the next save/push to permanently overwrite all stored overrides.
findings.evidence: `lib/style-guide-admin.js:1363` snapshots `snap.wsState` prior to `githubApiJson` network I/O (`lines 1455-1635`), then calls `writeWorkspaceState(storageDir, nextWsState)` (`line 1666`) using stale `snap.wsState.overrides_by_id`. `lib/style-guide-admin.js:346-348`: `catch { return emptyState(); }` with zero logging or error propagation.
findings.expected_behavior: All `save`, `reset`, and `push` mutations on `workspace-state.json` must serialize critical sections (via an in-process async mutex + PostgreSQL `pg_advisory_xact_lock`), `push` must re-read fresh `workspace-state.json` before recording `last_github_push` so concurrent `overrides_by_id` edits are preserved, and `readWorkspaceState` must quarantine/fail loudly (`500 STYLE_GUIDE_STATE_CORRUPT`) rather than returning `emptyState` when an existing `workspace-state.json` fails JSON parsing.
findings.actual_condition: Concurrent admin saves during a GitHub push are silently lost, and any partial/corrupted `workspace-state.json` resets all 103 workspace overrides to empty without warning.
findings.impact: Silent permanent loss of administrator Style Guide work on staging/hosted servers.
findings.root_cause: File-backed `workspace-state.json` mutations lacked concurrency locking across async network boundaries and treated `ENOENT` identically to `SyntaxError` in `readWorkspaceState`.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add an in-process promise mutex around `workspace-state.json` read-modify-write sections, re-load current `workspace-state.json` after GitHub push completes so only `last_github_push` (and monotonic `revision`) is updated without clobbering newer `overrides_by_id`, and distinguish `err.code === "ENOENT"` from corrupt-file errors in `readWorkspaceState`.
implementation_steps: In `lib/style-guide-admin.js:329-349`, return `emptyState()` ONLY when `err.code === "ENOENT"`; on JSON parse or I/O failure, throw a `StyleGuideAdminError` (`500`, `STYLE_GUIDE_STATE_CORRUPT`) and preserve the file untouched for operator recovery.

Introduce a module-level `withWorkspaceLock(storageDir, fn)` async queue serializing `saveStyleGuideAdminUpdates`, `resetStyleGuideAdminDecisions`, and the state-commit step of `pushStyleGuideWorkspaceToGithub`.

At the end of `pushStyleGuideWorkspaceToGithub` (`lines 1650-1668`), acquire `withWorkspaceLock`, re-read the latest `wsState` from disk, and merge `last_github_push: pushRecord` (keeping `pushed_at_revision: snap.wsState.revision` so newly saved edits during the push remain flagged as unpushed!).
findings.regression_risks: Recording `pushed_at_revision: snap.wsState.revision` when concurrent saves bumped `wsState.revision` ensures `unpushed_changes_since_last_push` accurately stays `true`!
findings.verification_steps: Add an integration test in `tests/style-guide-admin.integration.cjs` using a delayed mock GitHub server where Admin B calls `/api/admin/style-guide/save` while Admin A's `/api/admin/style-guide/push` is in flight, asserting Admin B's override survives and `unpushed_changes_since_last_push === true`.

findings.title: Emergency BITESHARK_PAUSE_WRITES=all omits newer customer/governance write surfaces, and X-BiteShark-Viewpoint: preview is unenforced on 33 of 34 admin-routes mutations
findings.subsystem: S3: Admin governance backend
findings.what_is_wrong: (1) `PAUSE_SCOPE_BY_FEATURE_KEY` in `lib/feature-controls.js:1161-1167` maps only 9 features, omitting `visit_journal`, `private_photos`, `suggested_trails`, and `admin_style_guide_workspace`, while `POST /api/community/report`, `/api/vendor/*`, `/api/invitations/accept`, `/api/onboarding/*`, and `/api/issues*` never call `enforceWritePause`. Consequently, `BITESHARK_PAUSE_WRITES=all` fails to freeze disk/DB writes during maintenance or disk-full incidents (including 5 MiB photo uploads!). (2) `server/admin-routes.js:615` defines `isPreviewViewpoint = String(req.headers['x-biteshark-viewpoint'] || '').trim().toLowerCase() === 'preview'`, yet checks it ONLY on `POST /api/community/report` (`line 2913`), leaving 33 other mutating routes in `server/admin-routes.js` (plus delegated exploration/profile routes) writable from read-only admin preview mode!
findings.evidence: `lib/feature-controls.js:1161-1167` lists only `booking_requests`, `vendor_dashboard_writes`, `pickup_pager_creation`, `pager_push_notifications`, `community_submissions`, `customer_profile`, `greatest_hits_collections`, `unlisted_collection_sharing`, and `shared_collection_photos`. In `server/admin-routes.js`, `isPreviewViewpoint` appears at `lines 615` and `2913` (`2` occurrences in `8,331` lines; `/api/admin/viewpoint` at `line 7318` is the viewpoint audit logger itself).

findings.title: 90-day vendor_application_evidence BYTEA retention and disabled-mode pager outbox/rate-limit scrubbing are completely unenforced
findings.subsystem: S3: Admin governance backend
findings.what_is_wrong: (1) `POST /api/onboarding/evidence` stores sensitive permit/license PDFs and images (`raw_bytes BYTEA`) with `retention_expires_at = now() + interval '90 days'` (`server/admin-routes.js:1873-1902`) and `/policies/privacy.html` promises 90-day retention, yet **zero** code in the entire repository deletes expired `vendor_application_evidence` rows or blocks downloading expired files in `GET /api/onboarding/evidence` (`lines 7981-8000`). (2) In `lib/pager-notifications.js:1705-1754`, when `BITESHARK_PUSH_PROVIDER_MODE=disabled` (the default on hosted staging!) or `pager_push_notifications` is paused/hidden, `processPushOutboxBatch` returns early *before* `purgeExpiredNotificationRecords` (`line 1864`), leaving expired subscription `p256dh`/`auth` keys and `pager_rate_limits` rows unpurged forever—and `biteshark-staging2` has no worker/maintenance systemd unit at all.
findings.evidence: Repository-wide search for `vendor_application_evidence` finds `INSERT` (`server/admin-routes.js:1873`), metadata `SELECT` (`lines 1572, 3357`), and download `SELECT ... raw_bytes` (`line 7981`, with no `AND retention_expires_at > now()` filter) — zero `DELETE` or `UPDATE raw_bytes = NULL` statements anywhere! In `lib/pager-notifications.js:1726-1754`, early `return` on `provider.mode === "disabled"` skips `await purgeExpiredNotificationRecords(dbAdapter, { now })` at `line 1864`. `deploy/systemd/` contains `truckly-staging-worker.service` (`primary`) and zero worker unit for `biteshark-staging2`.
findings.expected_behavior: `GET /api/onboarding/evidence` must reject downloads once `retention_expires_at <= now()`, background maintenance must purge expired `vendor_application_evidence` bytes and run `purgeExpiredNotificationRecords` regardless of `BITESHARK_PUSH_PROVIDER_MODE`, and `staging2` should include a maintenance/worker unit.
findings.actual_condition: Uploaded business permits/IDs (`BYTEA`) accumulate indefinitely in PostgreSQL backups and remain downloadable forever past 90 days; push keys and rate-limit buckets are never scrubbed when Web Push is disabled.
findings.impact: Direct contradiction of published Privacy Policy retention commitments, unnecessary sensitive document retention in PostgreSQL, and unbounded table growth.
findings.root_cause: `retention_expires_at` was populated on `INSERT` without implementing read-time expiry checks or adding `vendor_application_evidence` purge SQL to the maintenance worker; `purgeExpiredNotificationRecords` was placed after early provider-mode exits.
findings.recommended_remediation: Enforce `retention_expires_at > now()` in `GET /api/onboarding/evidence`, execute `purgeExpiredNotificationRecords` *before* the `provider.mode === "disabled"` early return in `processPushOutboxBatch`, add expired `vendor_application_evidence` purging to the periodic maintenance cycle, and add `deploy/systemd/biteshark-staging2-worker.service`.
implementation_steps: In `server/admin-routes.js:7981-8000`, add `AND e.retention_expires_at > now()` (or return `410 EVIDENCE_RETENTION_EXPIRED` when `retention_expires_at <= now()`).

In `lib/pager-notifications.js:1715-1755`, invoke `await purgeExpiredNotificationRecords(dbAdapter, { now })` prior to returning early when `provider.mode === "disabled"` or feature state is paused/hidden.

Add a bounded cleanup step (`DELETE FROM vendor_application_evidence WHERE retention_expires_at <= now()` on terminal `approved`/`rejected` applications, or scrubbing expired rows) inside `api/pager/worker.js` / `scripts/run-pager-worker.cjs`, and commit `deploy/systemd/biteshark-staging2-worker.service`.
findings.dependencies: Ensure `app_role` has `DELETE` (or scoped `UPDATE`) privileges on `vendor_application_evidence` or add via additive migration `030` (`migrations/018` grants `SELECT, INSERT, DELETE`—verify in `migrations/018_admin_portal_onboarding_moderation_issues.sql`!).
findings.regression_risks: Verify whether open/pending applications older than 90 days should retain metadata while purging `raw_bytes` or return `410` asking the applicant to re-upload fresh evidence.
findings.verification_steps: Add integration tests in `tests/legal-readiness.integration.cjs` and `tests/pager-notifications.integration.cjs` backdating `retention_expires_at` (`410` on download + purged by worker) and verifying `purgeExpiredNotificationRecords` runs under `BITESHARK_PUSH_PROVIDER_MODE=disabled`.

findings.title: Swallowed SessionEligibilityError turns normal revocations into 500/503 alerts, and unvalidated related_review_id in POST /api/issues causes 500 FK crash & private-post oracle
findings.subsystem: S3: Admin governance backend
findings.what_is_wrong: (1) `handleCustomerProfileRoute` (`server/customer-profile-routes.js:665-686`) catches `SessionEligibilityError` (`401` revoked / `403` age gate) and `PhotoStorageError` (`404` missing file in `readAdminReportedSharedPhoto`), returning `500 PROFILE_INTERNAL_ERROR` (`retryable: true`) and logging false `error` incidents. (2) `GET /api/account/context` (`server/admin-routes.js:854-861`) similarly catches `SessionEligibilityError` and returns `503` + logs `ACCOUNT_CONTEXT_DB_FAILURE`. (3) `POST /api/issues` (`server/admin-routes.js:2360, 2520`) checks only `UUID_RE.test(relatedReviewId)` without verifying existence or visibility in `community_reviews`: nonexistent UUIDs crash with unhandled PostgreSQL `23503` FK violation (`500`), while another user's private `pending`/`rejected` post UUID succeeds with `201 Created`!
findings.evidence: Compare `server/customer-exploration-routes.js:199-200` (`// Re-throw SessionEligibilityError ... throw err;`) against `server/customer-profile-routes.js:666` (`const status = err instanceof CustomerProfileDomainError ? err.status : 500;`) and `server/admin-routes.js:854-861` (`catch (err) { recordServerDiagnostic(... "ACCOUNT_CONTEXT_DB_FAILURE" ...); return sendJson(503, ...); }`). In `server/admin-routes.js:2360, 2520`, `related_review_id` is inserted directly into `support_issues` (`REFERENCES community_reviews(id)` in `migrations/018:335`).
findings.expected_behavior: `SessionEligibilityError` must propagate to `server/app.js:1411-1420` (returning `401 SESSION_REVOKED` or `403 AGE_ASSESSMENT_REQUIRED` with zero `5xx` diagnostics), `PhotoStorageError` must map to its HTTP status (`404`/`503`/`507`), and `POST /api/issues` must verify `related_review_id` exists in `community_reviews` AND is either `status = "approved"` or authored by `req.user.id` (else `400 INVALID_RELATED_REVIEW`).
findings.actual_condition: Mid-request sign-outs/revocations produce `500`/`503` errors and false incident alerts, and `POST /api/issues` acts as an existence oracle for unpublished community posts while crashing with `500` on invalid UUIDs.
findings.impact: False-positive production outage alerts, retry storms (`retryable: true` on `401`), `500` crashes, and cross-user private review UUID probing.
findings.root_cause: Over-broad `catch (err)` blocks in `customer-profile-routes.js` and `/api/account/context` swallowed typed domain errors, and `POST /api/issues` skipped pre-insert FK/visibility validation on `related_review_id`.
findings.recommended_remediation: Re-throw `SessionEligibilityError` in `server/customer-profile-routes.js` and `GET /api/account/context`, map `PhotoStorageError` in `sendProfileError`, and validate `related_review_id` visibility (`status = 'approved' OR author_id = $2`) inside `POST /api/issues` (returning uniform `400` on missing or unauthorized UUIDs).
implementation_steps: In `server/customer-profile-routes.js:665` and `server/admin-routes.js:854`, add `if (err instanceof SessionEligibilityError || err?.isSessionEligibilityError) throw err;`, and map `err instanceof PhotoStorageError` in `sendProfileError` (`lines 169-188`).

In `server/admin-routes.js:2440-2525` (`POST /api/issues`), if `relatedReviewId` is provided, query `SELECT 1 FROM community_reviews WHERE id = $1 AND (status = 'approved' OR author_id = $2)` inside the transaction and return `400 { error: "Referenced community post was not found." }` when empty.
findings.regression_risks: Administrators filing internal issues referencing a `pending`/`rejected` post can also be permitted via `OR ctx.canAccessAdminPortal`.
findings.verification_steps: Add tests in `tests/customer-profile-sharing.integration.cjs` and `tests/support-feedback.integration.cjs` verifying mid-tx session revocation returns `401` (not `500`/`503`) and `POST /api/issues` with a random UUID or another user's `pending` review returns `400` (not `500` or `201`).

findings.title: Mismatched pager worker summary keys (failed/sent vs failed_permanent/delivered) silently disable batch failure diagnostics and degraded heartbeats
findings.subsystem: S5: Pager notifications, Web Push worker & diagnostics
findings.what_is_wrong: `processPushOutboxBatch` (`lib/pager-notifications.js:1785-1788`) returns `{ processed, delivered, retried, failed_permanent, suppressed, ... }`. However, BOTH `api/pager/worker.js` (`lines 127, 148`) and `scripts/run-pager-worker.cjs` (`lines 146-147, 243`) read `Number(out.failed || 0)` and `Number(out.sent || 0)`—keys that do not exist (`undefined -> 0`)! Consequently, `failedCount > 0 && sentCount === 0` is **permanently false**, `PUSH_DELIVERY_BATCH_FAILURE` diagnostics are never recorded, and worker heartbeats always report `worker_status: "ok"` (`last_error_code: null`) even during 100% permanent push delivery failure.
findings.evidence: `lib/pager-notifications.js:1785-1788`: returns `delivered`, `retried`, `failed_permanent`, `suppressed` (no `sent`, no `failed`). `api/pager/worker.js:127, 148`: `const failedCount = Number(out?.failed || 0); const sentCount = Number(out?.sent || 0);` and `workerStatus: failedCount > 0 && sentCount === 0 ? 'degraded' : 'ok'`. `scripts/run-pager-worker.cjs:146-147, 243` repeats the exact same `out.failed` / `out.sent` bug.
findings.expected_behavior: `api/pager/worker.js` and `scripts/run-pager-worker.cjs` must read `out.failed_permanent` (plus `out.retried` when evaluating complete batch failure) and `out.delivered` so total push delivery outages emit `PUSH_DELIVERY_BATCH_FAILURE` and mark the worker heartbeat `degraded`.
findings.actual_condition: Dead code branch on every worker tick: permanent VAPID/FCM/APNs push delivery failures look 100% healthy (`worker_status: "ok"`) in `/admin` Diagnostics & Readiness.
findings.impact: Complete blind spot in operational alerting and readiness monitoring when Web Push delivery breaks in staging or production.
findings.root_cause: Field rename drift between `lib/pager-notifications.js` (`delivered` / `failed_permanent`) and its two callers (`api/pager/worker.js`, `scripts/run-pager-worker.cjs`) without a unit assertion on degraded worker heartbeats.
findings.recommended_remediation: Update `api/pager/worker.js` and `scripts/run-pager-worker.cjs` to read `Number(out?.failed_permanent || 0)` (and consider `Number(out?.retried || 0)` when `delivered === 0`) and `Number(out?.delivered || 0)`.
implementation_steps: In `api/pager/worker.js:126-152`, compute `const failedCount = Number(out?.failed_permanent ?? out?.failed ?? 0); const retriedCount = Number(out?.retried || 0); const sentCount = Number(out?.delivered ?? out?.sent ?? 0);` and trigger `degraded` / `PUSH_DELIVERY_BATCH_FAILURE` when `(failedCount > 0 || retriedCount > 0) && sentCount === 0` (with `failed_permanent > 0` at `error`/`warn` severity).
Update `scripts/run-pager-worker.cjs:145-150, 242-260` identically so `--direct-db` mode matches HTTP loopback mode.
findings.regression_risks: Ensure transient single-item retries (`retried > 0`) when other items succeed (`sentCount > 0`) remain `ok` so a single flaky browser endpoint does not mark the whole worker degraded.
findings.verification_steps: Add an integration test in `tests/pager-notifications.integration.cjs` simulating a `400`/`403` permanent push provider rejection and asserting `PUSH_DELIVERY_BATCH_FAILURE` is recorded and `worker_heartbeats.worker_status === "degraded"`.

findings.title: Swallowed ROLLBACK errors in runtime-adapter and lib/db-tx.js call client.release() without error flag, returning poisoned connections to pg.Pool
findings.subsystem: S2: HTTP server core, routing, api/* handlers & DB adapter
findings.what_is_wrong: In `node-postgres` (`pg`), when a query or `ROLLBACK` fails on a checked-out `PoolClient` (for example due to `statement_timeout`, socket reset, or broken protocol state), calling `client.release()` with no argument returns the broken/in-aborted-transaction client back to the idle `pg.Pool` instead of destroying it (`client.release(rollbackErr || true)`). Both `packages/runtime-adapter/index.js` and `lib/db-tx.js` swallow `ROLLBACK` failures (`catch {}`) and call bare `client.release()`.
findings.evidence: `packages/runtime-adapter/index.js:94-110`: `catch (err) { try { await client.query('ROLLBACK'); } catch {} throw err; } finally { client.release(); }`. `lib/db-tx.js:215-223`: `catch (err) { try { await client.query('ROLLBACK'); } catch { // Ignore rollback error if connection dropped } throw err; } finally { client.release(); }`.
findings.expected_behavior: Track `let destroyClient = false;` inside `try/catch`; if `ROLLBACK` throws (or `COMMIT` throws a transport/protocol error), set `destroyClient = rollbackErr || true` and invoke `client.release(destroyClient)` in `finally` so `pg.Pool` evicts and replaces the broken connection.
findings.actual_condition: If `ROLLBACK` fails on one of the 8 pool connections (`DB_POOL_MAX = 8`), the poisoned connection is returned to the pool and can fail subsequent unrelated requests (`25P02 current transaction is aborted` or stale session state).
findings.impact: Cascading database request failures and potential connection-state contamination on an 8-connection VPS pool.
findings.root_cause: Standard `pg.Pool` pitfall: `client.release()` only destroys a broken client when passed a truthy error argument.
findings.recommended_remediation: Pass the rollback error (`client.release(releaseErr)`) to `client.release(...)` in both `packages/runtime-adapter/index.js` and `lib/db-tx.js`.
implementation_steps: In `lib/db-tx.js:180-225`, declare `let releaseErr = false;`, set `releaseErr = rbErr || true` inside `catch (rbErr)` around `ROLLBACK`, and call `client.release(releaseErr)` in `finally`.
Apply the identical `let releaseErr = false;` -> `client.release(releaseErr)` guard in `packages/runtime-adapter/index.js:85-112`.
findings.regression_risks: None; healthy transactions and normal SQL errors where `ROLLBACK` succeeds still call `client.release(false)` and reuse the pooled socket.
findings.verification_steps: Add a unit test in `tests/backend-hardening.integration.cjs` with a mock `dbAdapter.connect()` whose `ROLLBACK` rejects and assert `client.release` was called with a truthy error argument.

findings.title: biteshark-staging2-api.service omits style-guide ReadWritePaths under ProtectSystem=strict, backup-staging2.sh is missing from Git, and push CI diff skips failing runtime suites
findings.subsystem: S10: Deploy, systemd, Nginx, CI/CD, dependencies & code-registry
findings.what_is_wrong: (1) `deploy/systemd/biteshark-staging2-api.service` sets `ProtectSystem=strict` (`line 31`) and `ReadWritePaths=-/var/lib/biteshark-staging2/customer-photos` (`line 39`), omitting `-/var/lib/biteshark-staging2/style-guide` (which IS present in `deploy/systemd/truckly-staging-api.service:39`!). Installing the committed systemd unit on `staging2` causes `EROFS: read-only file system` on Style Guide saves/pushes. (2) Both `deploy/systemd/biteshark-staging2-backup.service:10` and `deploy/bin/biteshark-staging2-ctl:56` execute `/usr/local/lib/biteshark-staging2/backup-staging2.sh`, which does not exist anywhere in the repository! (3) `.github/workflows/truckly-source-review.yml:195-206` computes `BASE_REF="$PUSH_BEFORE"` on `push` events and omits `.github/workflows` and `package.json` from `RUNTIME_DIFF`: pushing a docs-only commit immediately after a broken runtime commit skips all 33 PostgreSQL/browser suites and marks the branch green.
findings.evidence: `deploy/systemd/biteshark-staging2-api.service:39`: `ReadWritePaths=-/var/lib/biteshark-staging2/customer-photos` vs `deploy/systemd/truckly-staging-api.service:39`: `ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/truckly-staging/customer-photos -/var/lib/truckly-staging/style-guide`. `deployFiles` inventory confirms only `deploy/backup/truckly-staging-backup.sh` exists (`backup-staging2.sh` is absent). `.github/workflows/truckly-source-review.yml:195-196, 204`: `BASE_REF="$PUSH_BEFORE"` and `RUNTIME_DIFF="$(git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" HEAD -- api lib server packages public migrations deploy scripts package-lock.json)"` (missing `.github/workflows` and `package.json`).
findings.expected_behavior: `biteshark-staging2-api.service` must include `-/var/lib/biteshark-staging2/style-guide` in `ReadWritePaths`; `backup-staging2.sh` (or parameterized `truckly-staging-backup.sh` wrapper) must be tracked in `deploy/backup/`; and `.github/workflows/truckly-source-review.yml` must include `.github/workflows` + `package.json` in `RUNTIME_DIFF` and always run full PostgreSQL/browser gates on pushes to integration branches (`working/biteshark-vps`, `main`).
findings.actual_condition: Re-provisioning `staging2` from committed `deploy/` files breaks Style Guide persistence (`EROFS`) and lacks `backup-staging2.sh`, while CI `push` jobs can turn green without re-running failed runtime suites.
findings.impact: Deployment reproducibility failure on `staging2`, unversioned backup script risk, and CI gate bypass on multi-commit pushes.
findings.root_cause: `truckly-staging-api.service` was updated with Style Guide `ReadWritePaths` while `biteshark-staging2-api.service` and `backup-staging2.sh` were patched directly on the host or omitted; CI optimized `push` runtime using `github.event.before` without guarding protected integration branches.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add `-/var/lib/biteshark-staging2/style-guide` to `deploy/systemd/biteshark-staging2-api.service`, commit `deploy/backup/backup-staging2.sh` (wrapping or sharing `truckly-staging-backup.sh` with staging2 defaults), and update `.github/workflows/truckly-source-review.yml` + `tests/vps-platform-contract.test.cjs`.
implementation_steps: Update `deploy/systemd/biteshark-staging2-api.service:39` to `ReadWritePaths=-/var/lib/biteshark-staging2/customer-photos -/var/lib/biteshark-staging2/style-guide`.

Commit `deploy/backup/backup-staging2.sh` (setting `BITESHARK_STYLE_GUIDE_STORAGE_DIR=/var/lib/biteshark-staging2/style-guide`, `PHOTO_STORAGE_DIR=/var/lib/biteshark-staging2/customer-photos`, and `DB_NAME=biteshark_staging2` before delegating to the shared encrypted backup logic).
In `.github/workflows/truckly-source-review.yml:195-209`, add `.github/workflows package.json` to `RUNTIME_DIFF` and force `run=true` on `push` events to `working/biteshark-vps` or `main`.

In `server/app.js` / `lib/standalone-auth.js:2496`, append `buildClearedAdminTestSessionCookie()` on `POST /api/auth/verify` responses.

Fix `server/admin-routes.js:944` to `Boolean(ctx.canAccessAdminPortal && isAdminTestCustomerAllowedInEnv(env))` and add `DELETE` statements for `community_reports`, `support_issues`, `community_reviews`, and `vendor_applications` authored by `SYNTHETIC_TEST_CUSTOMER_USER_ID` in `lib/admin-test-customer.js:564-585`.
